[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35321477/29fbfba1284ac8f6c1d4ddbf7f25d6edca18d63b.png[/img]

Back when Rise was first in development it was very flight-centric ... the idea that we could go from orbit all the way down to the ground (without cut-scenes, etc) was pretty revolutionary and quite taxing on the technology of the time (almost 20 years ago!). notes.title: Revenue (Ticketed) Passengers
notes.notes:
Some of you may recall years ago that we had an artificial demand between Deois and the orbiting facilities as a way to earn revenue as a player. 

At some point we started tracking colonists individually (name, relationships, dietary restrictions, etc) and that old system was broken.

We finally circled back to get the ticketed passenger system back up and running - with a number of notable enhancements!

Laborers (employed colonists) accrue vacation time. They also each have a "desire" to travel which varies from person to person. Once they have enough vacation banked and they get the impulse to book a trip they then look at our new TripAdvisorLike system which sorts destinations based on a number of variables. It could be facilities (like casinos or parks) or themes (like agriculture) or just going from a bustling metropolis (Deois) to a quieter, simpler Amish community (like Lancaster). [b]Only colonies that have a public airfield (requires 4 letter identifier) are eligible.[/b]

Once the laborer (and their family, if they chose) are ready, they will appear on this "Passenger Demand" matrix which is on the Player Portal:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35321477/ae1de35dfacce65552c7b41c60b649496639b095.png[/img]

When you are at the point of origin, you can pick up passengers headed to multiple destinations. For example, picking up at Alphaville (VALP) there are people wanting to go to Deois (VDEO) and Easydock (TAC). I can say "VDEO,TAC" and I will load passengers to both destinations (meaning we now support mixed destinations!). [b]Passenger PODS are required for these operations as revenue passengers are prohibited from sitting in the jump seat or crew seats).[/b] The whole idea here is that the passengers to TAC are on a "through flight" which means they deplane briefly at Deois before heading to TAC (like a connecting flight). [b]Each stopover will reduce the ticket price![/b]

You will also notice that the flight attendant will make cabin announcements any time revenue passengers are on board!

Before going live, the ticketed passenger system was used for a huge "reunification" project where we corrected hundreds of families being separated over the years (i.e. employee at Alphaville but wife is in Kansas and their kid who is not old enough to work is in Deois!).

These are mapped on the keyboard on the "(" and ")" keys. There are 5 settings at 25% increments (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). The spoiler panels deflect upwards at about 50 degrees. Numerous CAS messages have been added (caution and advisory) as well as T/O CONFIG checks.

notes.title: Cabin Pressure and Bypass Ratios
notes.notes:
"skippy" was flying along in a T-19 near the operational vertical limit (service ceiling) and got distracted. He unknowningly continued to climb and suddely, without warning, the pressure vessel popped. His death was surely painless.

Many of our technologies and most of our regulations stemmed from disasters like these. 

We initially reported some deficiencies in this area of cabin pressure and pressure regulation and CAS messaging back in 2020 but
hadn't sat down to fully flesh out the implications of operating on the surface at 2.5+ bar and going to orbit and back while maintaining passenger comfort. 

Ultimately we decided on some pretty substantial engineering to allow 2+ bar pressure differentials. The orbiting space stations are at 1 bar. Ground dwellers who venture out of their habitats would experience high Nitrogen levels at 2.5 bar. We imagine they wouldn't build the structures to sustain a pressure differential but would enjoy more normal partial pressure of Nitrogen by substituting other inert gases. Those that have to work outside would be called "Narcs" because of the subtle but real threat of Nitogen Narcosis at that pressure. 

If surface destination set it will gradually (500 fpm for comfort) adjust the cabin pressure to meet the destination.
If they have no destination and are below 10km it will use radar altimeter to determine a touchdown elevation and equivalent ISA pressure.
If they are above 10km or have a non-surface destination then it will use 1 bar.

Oh and while we were in there we added the bypass ratios to the engine definitions for every vehicle type!

notes.title: 2.2.18.8 Dock Telemetry Update
notes.notes:
Biggest change is the dock telemetry. We used to calculate the position once per frame based on an epoch and the orbital parameters. Now the server actually runs these calculations and progresses the orbit and synchronizes the epoch with the client when you log in! This was done to reduce slight precision errors we have seen develop over the last 15 years since the server was started. It also lightens the computational load that the client is responsible for!

We had actually baked in support for NaturalPoint's TrackIR product back in the early development of Rise but the support was never carried over to game client 2.0 as we had no active players (that we knew about at least) that used head tracking.

The other day I was talking to a player and he mentioned head tracker support. Literally within 48 hours we had released support for head trackers on Steam. And it is a step in the right direction for our VR initiative!

The user in question is using [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/opentrack.mirror/]OpenTrack [/url] which is a free software that you can use to configure and "shape" your existing head tracker, VR headset, or [url=http://www.facetracknoir.nl/]FaceTrackNoIR[/url].

notes.title: Player Generated Roads
notes.notes:
Players start out with barely a shirt on their back ... two cents to rub together ... you get the idea. But you do have a car ... not that you can get very far from Deois without getting stuck in the mud!

With all of the colonies surrounding Deois, new players miss out on many [url=https://deois.risetvp.com]lucrative opportunities[/url] due to the lack of improved surfaces to drive on. 

We recently added colony territories to aid in the management of colonies and their resources. Exposing the colonies and their territories on the [url=https://portal.risetvp.com]Player Portal[/url] made it a straight-forward tweak to allow construction of road segments through the same interface.

Each road segment costs 11,065 MT of grade C (common) materials. You can read more about the restrictions and requirements on the [url=https://www.risetvp.com/Roads]wiki[/url].

notes.title: Colony Management Updates
notes.notes:
We recently upgraded the [url=http://rise.reskin.us/portal]player portal[/url] to [url=https://openlayers.org/]OpenLayers 6[/url] and added a feature that creates territories where multiple user colonies exist. 

For example, Alphaville (to the east of the capital city Deois) has many farms, mines, townships, and an airfield. That territory is now considered Alphaville proper and the influence/size of the territory is based on the population.

Colonies that are within the same territory (partitioned by owner) enjoy the added benefit of shared/pooled resources. That means the old adjacent colony transfers system is gone! No more worrying about the mine right next to a farm starving to death! And now if someone lands at [b]any[/b] of your colonies in the territory they will have access to load/unload/buy/sell commodities from the collective pool.

Soon you will also be able to change the buy/sell pricing, minimum (reserve) and maximum quantities for each commodity at the territory level through the portal. 

We feel these changes enhance the gameplay by minimizing micromanagement needed for colonies so you can concentrate on flying!

notes.title: An "Explosive" Update
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35321477/6a842046b8d23e413732cb1fc7c8b687b0a63e53.png[/img]

After months of research and reading theoretical mathematics papers explaining how explosions propagate through open air we now have added the realistic explosion of the “Longarm" Missiles, the “Munitions" cargo container, and the "Auxiliary Fuel" container. 

The Longarms have been determined to each have an equivalent yield of 570 kg of TNT.

Munitions containers explode with a yield based on the quantity of Longarms they are carrying. 

An Auxilary Fuel container that is full and dropped from height or shot with a Longarm will explode with an equivalent yield of 745 MT of TNT

While working on the Longarm explosive payload the question was asked “How much damage will 12 kg of Iagreous fuel do?”. We then took the MJ/kg and converted the energy to kg of TNT.  Approximately 15 minutes into the yield calculations someone asked “What happens if you explode a full Auxiliary Fuel container?” That brought out how dangerous it would be to shoot a full Auxiliary Fuel container. 

The next steps will be to move and toss the offline vehicles affected by the explosions as well as calculate impacts between two vehicles.

notes.title: T-19 Stratomaster Update
notes.notes:
We have cleared many hurdles but the replacement for the T-2 Stratoranger aircraft is getting ready for flight testing. Preliminary numbers confirm that it is sleeker and safer than it's predecessor. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35321477/94e42536b5ee0b88665411ce0d3b4fc3e78c3514.png[/img]

To give you an idea of the process we come up with a requirement (VTOL vs. wheeled, air vs. space capable, cargo capacity) and a preliminary design that fits those specifications. Then the artist constructs it in our proprietary modeling program which does baked lighting (for speed), rigging (for animations), and a virtual wind tunnel (for aerodynamics). We then take the numbers we come up with and plug them into the attached spreadsheet. This can be iterative as the CG might need to be adjusted or surfaces that are designated as control surfaces expanded. Finally (the stage we are at now) we have numbers we can plug into the game engine and let our QA take it for a test drive in the simulator. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35321477/32bfa5b5bab01b5ed97345441194391fec89de4a.png[/img]

If there are no red flags we might be seeing these flown by test pilots in the game within a week!

[b]Steam users will be given vouchers to upgrade their tired T-1 Stratoranger to the new T-19 Stratomaster[/b]

notes.title: CAS Upgrades
notes.notes:
[b]What is CAS?[/b]

The crew-alerting system (CAS) is used in place of the annunciator panel on older systems. Rather than signaling a system failure by turning on a light behind a translucent button, failures are shown as a list of messages in a small window near the other EICAS indications.

[b]What has changed?[/b]

We moved the "acknowledge" key binding from "Q" to the "Scroll Lock" key. In addition, we wired up the scroll lock light to flash with the CAS messages for an immersive effect. Finally, we added "inhibits" to eliminate distractions during the most critical phases of flight (takeoff and landing).
